newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin sees job creation momentum.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees job creation momentum.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Friday there was clear momentum in jobs creation in Canada despite "very disappointing" unemployment figures for September.
He added that it takes time for interest rate reductions to translate into new jobs.
"There is clearly a positive momentum in terms of job creation," he told reporters outside parliament.
"There's obviously a lag time between the interest rate reduction and when the jobs are created," Martin said.
"A little over a year ago, (short-term) interest rates were at 8-1/2 percent. Today they're under four. You've really got to give that time to take place."

Martin added that while interest rate cuts were an essential condition for job creation, they were not all that was required. He cited the need for trade financing, trade missions, investment in research and development, working with provinces on training and "essentially focusing on those areas where Canada can improve its productivity."

"We've got to understand that we lost a decade, more than a decade. Productivity in Canada began to decline in 1973 and it's only in the last two to three years that it's begun gradually to increase," Martin said.

"So there aren't going to be any magic solutions here. But I can tell you that this country is better positioned for job creation and growth than any other G-7 country," he said, referring to the Group of Seven top industrialized nations.
"Any economist will tell you, and they're all projecting, that there will be substantially improved job creation as in fact those interest rates begin to plug in."
The government reported on Friday that the unemployment rate jumped to 9.9 percent from 9.4 percent in September as the economy lost 47,000 jobs.
